harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across the three RHEL 10 nodes: node1 as writable primary, node2 and node3 as read-only async standbys (via pg_basebackup -R with a replicator role and streaming replication slots). Opened firewalld's postgresql service on all nodes to permit inter-node connections. Verified writes on the primary propagate to both standbys and that standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), confirming boot_id change on each node and full replication/data recovery after each restart, ending with a final write-then-read-on-both-standbys check post all restarts.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/repo/sudo access on node1-3 (RHEL 10, AppStream repo, passwordless sudo)
Installed postgresql-server/postgresql-contrib 16.14 on all three nodes (retried node1 after a transient GPG key parse race)
Initialized primary DB on node1 with postgresql-setup --initdb

Configured node1 postgresql.conf (listen_addresses, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots, hot_standby) and pg_hba.conf (scram-sha-256 for replication and app users from the cluster subnet)
Started PostgreSQL on node1; created replicator role with a randomly generated password (passed via secret_env, never in tool commands or this report)
Created appdb database and demo table with baseline rows on node1
Opened firewalld postgresql service on node1 (found blocking 5432, caused initial 'No route to host')
Wiped node2/node3 data dirs and ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 to build standbys with standby.signal + primary_conninfo
Opened firewalld postgresql service on node2/node3, started PostgreSQL on both as standbys
Verified pg_stat_replication shows both standbys streaming; verified pg_is_in_recovery=true on standbys and write rejection; verified insert on primary replicates to both standbys
Captured baseline boot_id and health/data proof on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, standby recovery state, row count, and resumed streaming on primary
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, standby recovery state, row count, and resumed streaming on primary

Restarted node1 (primary) via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=false, row count, and both standbys reconnected/streaming
Performed final post-all-restarts write on primary and confirmed it replicated to both standbys

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as writable streaming-replication primary with wal_level/replication settings and replicator role
evidence.summary: postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf updated for replication, service started, replicator role created, appdb/demo table with baseline rows created on node1

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via pg_basebackup streaming from node1
evidence.summary: firewall opened, pg_basebackup -R succeeded on both nodes producing standby.signal + primary_conninfo, PostgreSQL started active on both

evidence.requirement: Replication is live and standbys are read-only
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication shows both nodes streaming; both standbys report pg_is_in_recovery=t and see baseline rows; node2 write attempt rejected with read-only transaction error

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Inserted 'post-replication-check' row on node1; row visible on both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 636556ce captured; reboot acknowledged; polled boot_id changed to b12b662d; postgresql active, still in recovery, row count intact, node1 shows node2 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7ef78016 captured; reboot acknowledged; polled boot_id changed to af9a0f07; postgresql active, still in recovery, row count intact, node1 shows node3 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2b19e976 captured; reboot acknowledged; polled boot_id changed to 984814e2; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=false (writable primary), row count intact, both standbys reconnected/streaming
After all three restarts, inserted 'post-restart-check' row on node1 and confirmed it appears on both node2 and node3
